paragraphs: Shimi bar Hiyya bar Rav. Rav visited the house of Rav Shimi bar Hiyya, his grandson: Hullin 101b [111b:14 in the checked edition]. He answered Rav: Yevamot 45a. Rav used to ask him, ‘Are you Shimi?’ Menahot 29a: Rashi explains that Rav asks in surprise, ‘Are you the one challenging me?’ Bekhorot 43b: Rashi explains, a great sage like you does not know how to resolve it? Niddah 24a: Rashi explains that he said it affectionately. ‘I heard that Rav did not raise his eyes and did not recognize him; this does not appear right, since he said this to no one else.’ Because of affection, since he was sharp-witted. Another explanation: Rav did not raise his eyes beyond four cubits, out of modesty, end of Menahot 110a. He did not remember that Rashi rejected this; see Bekhorot 43b. He sat at a meal with Rav and Shmuel: Berakhot 47a.
